title: Grateful Dead Live at Boston Tea Party on 1969-12-29

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording is clear and decent while the New Year's Eve ’69 Boston show delivers high‑energy performances with standout versions of “Dancing In The Streets,” “Mason’s Children,” and “Easy Wind.”
ai_review.review: The mix is praised as crisp with only minor quirks – vocals sit a touch high and a mic‑grab incident adds some chaos – but overall the soundboard capture is solid. Musically the band is tight, rolling through a vibrant set that highlights a 15‑minute “Dancing In The Streets,” a fiery “Mason’s Children,” and an especially sweet “Easy Wind,” keeping the energy high throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently strong praise for both performance (high‑energy, tight playing, several standout songs) and recording quality (good mix, clear soundboard). Weighted average of show (≈4) and recording (≈4.5) yields ~4.2.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Decent clarity with a crisp mix; vocals are slightly high, occasional mic‑grab noise, but overall listenable without major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: New Year's Eve run starts chill with Rain & Snow and Mama Tried, builds momentum through Easy Wind and Uncle John’s Band, peaks with a hot High Time and Mason's Children, and closes on a spirited Good Lovin' that sets the mood for the remainder of the night.

band_member_comments.Keys: Thick "TC" keyboard runs noted; Pigpen’s vocal shouts and organ work highlighted throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill's drumming described as solid; Mickey Hart mentioned in a comment about his later diminishing role.
